key_insight: Increasing infrared excitation intensity drives a Mott-like crossover in 2D (BA)₂PbI₄ from exciton-dominated behavior toward a dense electron–hole plasma, alongside a switch from saturable to reverse saturable absorption.
engineering_relevance: The switchable nonlinear optical response could support infrared all-optical devices, although the abstract demonstrates neither solar-cell performance nor an AI method.
method: Probe nonlinear absorption and refraction using femtosecond Z-scan measurements at 1030 nm.
Excite near the two-photon resonance of the excitonic transition.
Track carrier dynamics using intensity-dependent transient absorption spectroscopy.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports intensity-dependent absorption switching and a long-lived carrier population above the estimated Mott density, supporting the proposed Mott-like transition.
watch_item: The Mott density is estimated, and practical operating thresholds, stability, and device-level performance are not quantified in the abstract.
paper_title: Intensity-driven Mott-like transition in a 2D Ruddlesden-Popper perovskite
